items.title: dell-5530 maintenance window: rotate leaked node token, re-parent orphaned Scheduled Task, decide auto-logon
items.description: One window closes three things at once. The node token was exposed in a transcript on 2026-09-09 and is still live (risk bounded to LAN: agent binds 192.168.1.250:8790, node not on tailnet). The agent is ALSO orphaned from its Scheduled Task (task state Ready, LastTaskResult 0x8007042B) so Stop-ScheduledTask is a no-op and RestartOnFailure gives no auto-restart. Costs all 6 ConPTY sessions - they are in-process children of the agent and cannot survive a restart by design. Runbook is in the multi-node memory note.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot sessions + each running claude's transcript id before shutdown
Graceful POST /v1/internal/shutdown (schtasks /end is a no-op on the orphan)
New token written to C:\Users\tranv\.terminal-mcp\node-agent.token AND controller node-agent-tokens.env
Start-ScheduledTask; task state shows Running and tracks the live agent
Old token returns 401, new token 200, verified from the node side
Decide BootTrigger vs LogonType=InteractiveToken (auto-logon) - do NOT switch to S4U without checking the show_on_desktop ConPTY path
Sessions recreated and claude --resume'd per snapshot

items.title: Rate-limit / lockout on node-agent bearer auth
items.description: Token comparison is constant-time but unbounded: an attacker on the LAN (or on any network a node is exposed to) can attempt tokens indefinitely. Found in the 2026-09-09 internet-connectivity audit.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated 401s from one source are throttled or locked out
Legitimate heartbeat traffic (20s interval) is never throttled
Lockout state cannot wedge a node permanently

items.title: Node token rotation and revocation mechanism
items.description: There is no rotation/revocation path today - rotating a token is a manual, per-node, restart-requiring edit of two files (proven twice on 2026-09-09: macbook rotated, dell-5530 deferred because its restart costs 6 sessions). Roadmap Phase 5 names this.
acceptance_criteria: A token can be rotated without hand-editing files on both sides
Revocation takes effect without a full node restart, or the restart cost is documented per platform
Old token is provably rejected afterwards

items.title: Validate node endpoint scheme: refuse plaintext http:// to a non-private host
items.description: config.py accepts any non-empty string as nodes.remote[].endpoint. A plaintext http:// endpoint pointed at a public host would send the bearer token in the clear on every request. RemoteNodeClient already verifies TLS correctly for https:// - only the scheme check is missing.
acceptance_criteria: http:// to a public address is refused at config load with a clear error
http:// to a private/LAN/overlay address still works (today's deployments)
https:// unaffected

items.title: terminal-mcp-doctor reports 'lan: not configured' while the service IS LAN-bound
items.description: The CLI reads its OWN environment, not the running service's, so describe_endpoints reports loopback-only even though the service is bound to 192.168.1.132 and 100.81.85.120. The dashboard route is correct because it runs in-process. describe_endpoints' docstring claims it 'always reflects what the RUNNING process actually resolved' - true for the dashboard, false for the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: doctor reports the bind addresses the live service actually has
Or the docstring/output is corrected to say it reflects the CLI's own env
No false 'not configured' when a LAN/overlay bind is active

items.title: Live remote-node auto-dispatch smoke test through the real RemoteNodeClient
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 1. Gate before config.queue.enabled can be turned on against any real lane. Needs 0 dropped / 0 duplicate dispatch across restart and reconnect. m910 is the low-risk candidate (tmux-backed, restart-safe since the KillMode fix); dell-5530 is not, its sessions cannot survive an agent restart.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-dispatch verified end-to-end against a real remote node
0 dropped and 0 duplicate dispatch across a controller restart
Same across a node reconnect

items.title: Direct-send reliability fix: deploy and live-reverify on dell-5530
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 7. Fix is shipped locally; verifying it is Windows-ConPTY-specific and needs a real dell-5530 restart, so it rides the same maintenance window as the token rotation.
acceptance_criteria: Fix running on dell-5530
Direct send verified live on a real Windows session

items.title: Internet node transport: outbound WSS node->controller (roadmap Phase 2)
items.description: The 2026-09-09 audit's core finding: the data plane is controller->node (inbound to the node), so a NAT'd node is visible-but-uncontrollable - heartbeat lands, dashboard shows ONLINE, every real operation fails. Overlay VPN (now unblocked) is a workaround, not a fix; outbound WSS removes the inbound requirement entirely and is the only option that scales past hand-configured peers.
acceptance_criteria: A node behind NAT with no inbound port is fully controllable
Reconnect/backoff across sleep, Wi-Fi change and IP change without manual re-registration
Tasks enqueued while offline auto-dispatch on reconnect with no duplicates

items.title: Node self-registration with an enrollment token
items.description: An unknown node_id heartbeat is refused NODE_NOT_FOUND, and dashboard onboarding health-probes the node, so onboarding needs controller->node reachability AND a manual controller-side action. The goal 'install agent, paste token, it appears' is not achievable today.
acceptance_criteria: A new machine can enroll with only an enrollment token
No inbound reachability to the node required at enrollment
Enrollment is auditable and the token is single-use or scoped

items.title: registry_list / registry_search are not fleet-aware
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 13. terminal_registry_reopen is fleet-aware and node_agent now exposes /v1/registry, but the list/search surfaces (MCP + dashboard Persistent Registry panel) remain local-node-only.
acceptance_criteria: registry_list/search span every online node
Dashboard Persistent Registry panel shows remote sessions
Per-node failure is tolerated like the other fleet reads

items.title: Codex --resume support for registry_reopen
items.description: REQUIREMENTS Backlog item 11. Claude has --resume wiring; Codex does not, so a recovered Codex session starts fresh. Relevant now that macbook and dell-5530 both run Codex.
acceptance_criteria: A recovered Codex session resumes its conversation
Resume is verified before success is reported (no fake resurrection)

items.title: macOS nodes report platform='linux' in the node registry
items.description: node_agent.py's heartbeat defaults platform='linux' and macOS uses that same path, so macbook is registered as linux. Cosmetic today but wrong for any platform-aware routing or capability decision later.
acceptance_criteria: A macOS node reports platform='macos' (or darwin) in the registry
Linux and Windows nodes unchanged
Dashboard/doctor show the real platform

items.title: Production session_registry is polluted with ~268 test-artifact rows
items.description: 268 of 513 rows are test session names (test-*, mcprec-*, lifecycle-*). Cause is known and documented in conftest: the live service observes test tmux sessions on the shared tmux server and records them. Harmless but noisy, and it makes the registry hard to read.
acceptance_criteria: Test-named rows cleaned out of the production registry
A documented periodic cleanup, or tests stop creating rows the live service picks up

items.title: Two pre-existing test_kill_reopen failures from stale tmux sessions
items.description: test_dashboard_kill_route_refuses_protected_session and test_dashboard_rename_route_refuses_protected_session fail on clean main too, with 'duplicate session: lifecycle-protected-dashboard-rename' - leftover sessions on the shared tmux server, not a code defect. They have been masking real signal in every full-suite run this session.
acceptance_criteria: Both pass on a clean checkout
The test cleans up or uniquifies its session name so it cannot collide again

items.title: Flaky tests under full-suite load
items.description: test_integration_loop::test_two_concurrent_loop_instances_never_double_merge_the_same_handoff, test_dashboard_nodes::test_nodes_list_shows_local_node_online_after_a_get and test_p0_hardening::test_prompt_injection_in_pane_output_remains_inert_data each failed once in a full run and passed in isolation on both the branch and clean main. Timing-sensitive; they cost real triage time repeatedly.
acceptance_criteria: Each is made deterministic or explicitly marked/quarantined
A full run is reproducibly green apart from known-skipped tests

items.title: Heartbeat replay protection (nonce/timestamp)
items.description: node_heartbeat authenticates the bearer token but has no nonce or timestamp, so a captured heartbeat can be replayed. Low impact today (LAN-only, and a heartbeat only writes metrics) but it is a real gap once nodes are on the internet.
acceptance_criteria: A replayed heartbeat is rejected
Clock skew tolerated sensibly

items.title: Audit rows are per-node, not centrally aggregated
items.description: Each node writes its own audit.db. There is no fleet-wide audit view, so answering 'who sent what, where' means reading N databases.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet-wide audit query across online nodes
Per-node failure tolerated like other fleet reads

items.title: Per-node config lineage requires a manual rebuild on every pull
items.description: m910's config derives from the Dell's config.yaml (rebuild on the new upstream base + re-apply 3 edits) while macbook's derives from config.example.yaml (preserve verbatim). Both are locally modified so every git pull refuses until config.yaml is checked out first. This is error-prone and was hand-done twice on 2026-09-09.
acceptance_criteria: Node-specific config is not a modified copy of a tracked file
A pull needs no manual config surgery
Existing per-node differences preserved

items.title: Review codex_yolo default (--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox)
items.description: SessionLifecycleConfig.codex_yolo defaults to True, so ANY deployment that never mentions the setting launches Codex with approvals and sandbox bypassed. Currently inert on m910/macbook (m910 has no codex; macbook now DOES, so it is live there). Decide whether the safe default should be False with an explicit opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Default decided deliberately and documented
If it stays True, the risk is stated where an operator will see it
Per-node override is easy
